# URLCode admin

> Operator-installed administration extension for URLCode, on top of the auth
> extension's service: users, sessions, roles, audit, registration approval,
> two-person cases, support impersonation, health. Alpha on npm. Apache-2.0.

Install: `npm install @jimhoyd/urlcode @jimhoyd/urlcode-ui @jimhoyd/urlcode-auth @jimhoyd/urlcode-admin`
then `npx urlcode init my-site --with auth,admin`.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only)
- `extensions.admin: { version: "1", config: {} }`
- A mount: `/admin/*: { extension: admin, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST] }`
- The operator wires `adminExtension({ service, csrfKey, projectSha256, authMount: '/account' })`
  in the same host file as `authExtension`, sharing one service and CSRF key.
- `urlcode-admin init --directory /absolute/site` writes project, host, keys and README.
- Presentation: screens are `admin/*` kit templates (`adminTemplates`, `adminUiTemplates`);
  with `ui` from `createUiExtension` (sources `[authCatalogue]`, extensions `[authUiTemplates, adminUiTemplates]`)
  they render through `ui.kit`, otherwise through the shared primitives in the console shell.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): install, build from reviewed sources, wiring, permissions, console operation, health, exports.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md), [threat model](THREAT-MODEL.md).
- [Implementation status](IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md): built and remaining. Precedes the spike.
- [Design spike](docs/SPIKE-ADMIN.md): the source plan.
- [Acceptance](ACCEPTANCE.md), [clean-project test](CLEAN-PROJECT-TEST.md), [UX review](UX-REVIEW.md): evidence.

## Do not guess
- Permissions are auth's names (`auth.users.read`, `auth.users.manage`, `auth.sessions.manage`,
  `auth.audit.read`, `auth.cases.manage`, `auth.users.impersonate`, ...); `*` is full.
  The spike's `admin.*` names do not exist.
- Every write needs a fresh session and a reason; hidden controls are not authorization.
- Impersonation needs service opt-in, its permission and a notification callback, and
  `withSupportBanner` around every application response before it is enabled.
- Role definitions are operator configuration, not console edits.
